messages.subject: Binomial model with offset
parts:
Hello list,

I am modelling my data with a binomial outcome:

yi,j ∼ Bin(pi,j , ni,j )
logit(pi,j ) = Xi,j + β + zi,j

where n is the number of success and p the number of trials.

Now, both n and p in my dataset are recorded at non constant intervals, and I suspect that the proportion of success is somewhat related with the exposure time.
I'd therefore like to add an offset term in my model, however I am not quite sure how the offset term would interact with the trials in the left hand side of the binomial likelihood in INLA.

Can anyone explain this to me?

Thanks

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Binomial model with offset
parts:
you can add an offset using

y ~ ... + offset(var) + ...

and then 'var' will be added as a constant in the formula.

about the second question: have you considered to view y_ij as Poisson
instead? then the expose time is just there in the mean, see 'E' in
the poisson definition.

H
